---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m5p1t0 ----------------------------
(* Warehouse robot fleet updating a shared task-count register by quorum vote.
   A robot stages a write against a snapshot of the register and gathers a
   quorum of robot approvals; the write commits only if the register still
   equals the snapshot, so a robot whose snapshot went stale must retry. A
   robot can crash silently, discarding its staged write; a crashed robot casts
   no votes. The register value always equals the number of applied writes. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots
Quorum == 2
MaxV == 2

VARIABLES reg, applied, snap, staged, votes, crashed

vars == <<reg, applied, snap, staged, votes, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in 0..MaxV
    /\ applied \in 0..MaxV
    /\ snap \in [Robots -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ staged \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ votes \in [Robots -> SUBSET Robots]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ snap = [b \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ staged = [b \in Robots |-> FALSE]
    /\ votes = [b \in Robots |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}

Stage(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ ~staged[b]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = reg]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, applied, crashed>>

Vote(b, w) ==
    /\ staged[b]
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ w \notin votes[b]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![b] = @ \cup {w}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, applied, snap, staged, crashed>>

Commit(b) ==
    /\ staged[b]
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(votes[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ snap[b] = reg
    /\ reg < MaxV
    /\ reg' = snap[b] + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, votes, crashed>>

Retry(b) ==
    /\ staged[b]
    /\ snap[b] # reg
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, applied, snap, votes, crashed>>

Crash(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {b}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, applied, snap, votes>>

Recover(b) ==
    /\ b \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, applied, snap, staged, votes>>

Compact ==
    /\ reg = MaxV
    /\ \A b \in Robots : ~staged[b]
    /\ reg' = 0
    /\ applied' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, staged, votes, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Robots : Stage(b)
    \/ \E b \in Robots, w \in Robots : Vote(b, w)
    \/ \E b \in Robots : Commit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Robots : Retry(b)
    \/ \E b \in Robots : Crash(b)
    \/ \E b \in Robots : Recover(b)
    \/ Compact

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == reg = applied
============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl: A warehouse robot fleet shares a task-count register that the robots update concurrently, with each update gated by quorum voting. A robot that wants to post an update first stages it, recording a snapshot of the register's current value and opening a fresh approval tally. Robots then vote to approve a staged update, and only a non-crashed robot's vote counts; the update may commit once a quorum of robots has approved it. On commit, the register is set to the staging robot's snapshot plus one, but only if the register still equals that snapshot; if a rival robot committed in the meantime, the snapshot is stale and the commit is refused, forcing the staging robot to retry from a fresh snapshot rather than overwrite the rival's update. A robot can crash silently at any moment, which discards whatever write it had staged and prevents it from voting; a crashed robot can later recover. When the register reaches its ceiling with nothing staged, the fleet compacts it back to zero along with the applied-write count. Because a stale commit is always rejected, no committed update is silently overwritten. The full action set is: stage a write, cast an approval vote, commit on quorum, retry after a stale snapshot, crash a robot, recover a robot, and compact at the ceiling. SAFETY PROPERTY: the register value always equals the number of updates that have been applied to it.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m7p3t1 ----------------------------
(* Hospital operating-room scheduler allocating rooms through a compare-and-swap
   register per room. A team claims a room by CAS-ing the register from Free to
   itself; a separate holdings map records what each team holds. Claim requests
   arrive over a reorderable pool. The register and holdings are kept coherent:
   if the holdings map says a team holds a room, the room's register names that
   same team, so no room is ever allocated to two teams. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Teams, Free
Slots == 1..2

VARIABLES reg, holds, requests, served

vars == <<reg, holds, requests, served>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Slots -> Teams \cup {Free}]
    /\ holds \in [Teams -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ requests \in SUBSET (Teams \X Slots)
    /\ served \in 0..6

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ holds = [t \in Teams |-> {}]
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ served = 0

Request(t, s) ==
    /\ <<t, s>> \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {<<t, s>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, holds, served>>

Claim(t, s) ==
    /\ <<t, s>> \in requests
    /\ reg[s] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {s}]
    /\ requests' = requests \ {<<t, s>>}
    /\ served' = (served + 1) % 7

Release(t, s) ==
    /\ reg[s] = t
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![t] = @ \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requests, served>>

Drop(t, s) ==
    /\ <<t, s>> \in requests
    /\ requests' = requests \ {<<t, s>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, holds, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams, s \in Slots : Request(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Teams, s \in Slots : Claim(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Teams, s \in Slots : Release(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in Teams, s \in Slots : Drop(t, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDouble ==
    \A s \in Slots, t \in Teams : (s \in holds[t]) => (reg[s] = t)
============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Teams = {t1, t2}
    Free = FREE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDouble
nl: A hospital operating-room scheduler allocates rooms to surgical teams using a compare-and-swap register attached to each room. Teams submit claim requests into a shared pool that does not preserve order, so requests may be serviced in any sequence. To claim a room, a team performs a compare-and-swap on that room's register: the claim succeeds only if the register currently reads Free, in which case it is swapped to name the claiming team. Alongside the registers, the scheduler keeps a holdings map recording which rooms each team holds; a successful claim both swaps the register and adds the room to the team's holdings, and releasing a room both resets the register to Free and removes the room from holdings. A pending request may also be dropped. Because a claim only succeeds against a Free register and the register and holdings map are always updated together, the holdings map never says a team holds a room whose register names a different team, so a room is never allocated to two teams. The full action set is: submit a claim request, claim a room by compare-and-swap, release a room, and drop a pending request. SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the holdings map records that a team holds a room, that room's register names exactly that team.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m1p4t0 ----------------------------
(* Airport baggage router with a bounded two-lane buffer. Push authority moves
   around a token ring: only the token-holding sorter node may push a bag, and
   only while a free slot remains. A node can crash silently; if it held the
   token, the token is lost and later regenerated to a live node. Buffered bags
   across both lanes plus free slots always equal the fixed capacity. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Nodes == 1..2
Lanes == 1..2
Cap == 3
None == 0
RingNext(n) == (n % 2) + 1

Buffered(b) == b[1] + b[2]

VARIABLES loaded, free, holder, crashed

vars == <<loaded, free, holder, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ loaded \in [Lanes -> 0..Cap]
    /\ free \in 0..Cap
    /\ holder \in {None} \cup Nodes
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Nodes

Init ==
    /\ loaded = [l \in Lanes |-> 0]
    /\ free = Cap
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ crashed = {}

Push(n, l) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ free > 0
    /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Pop(l) ==
    /\ loaded[l] > 0
    /\ loaded' = [loaded EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

PassToken(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = RingNext(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, free, crashed>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ holder' = IF holder = n THEN None ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, free>>

Regenerate(n) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, free, crashed>>

Recover(n) ==
    /\ n \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, free, holder>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, l \in Lanes : Push(n, l)
    \/ \E l \in Lanes : Pop(l)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Regenerate(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Recover(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BufferCoherent == Buffered(loaded) + free = Cap
============================================================================

INVARIANT BufferCoherent
nl: An airport baggage router feeds a bounded sorting buffer split into two lanes. Push authority is serialized by a token ring of sorter nodes: a single token circulates, and only the node currently holding the token may push a bag into a lane, and only while at least one free buffer slot remains. Pushing a bag consumes a free slot, and popping a bag from a lane returns its slot to the free pool. A sorter node can crash silently at any time; if the crashed node was holding the token, the token is lost, and a lost token is later regenerated to some live, non-crashed node. A crashed node can recover and rejoin the ring, and the token holder may also pass the token onward. Because every push moves a slot from the free pool into a lane and every pop moves it back, the buffered bags across both lanes plus the free slots always equal the buffer's fixed capacity, so the buffer is never overfilled. The full action set is: push a bag, pop a bag, pass the token, crash a node, regenerate a lost token, and recover a node. SAFETY PROPERTY: the total buffered bags across both lanes plus the number of free slots always equals the buffer's fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m6p2t5 ----------------------------
(* Car-wash conveyor line. Cars occupy three cyclic slots. Advancing a car one
   slot forward normally requires a valid, unexpired lease on the conveyor
   drive; the lease is granted to one controller at a time and lapses as the
   clock advances. A privileged admin can force an advance without a lease.
   Every advance only moves a car to the next slot, so the car total is
   conserved. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, None
Slots == 0..2
Total == 3
MaxT == 3

VARIABLES load, leaseOwner, leaseExp, clock

vars == <<load, leaseOwner, leaseExp, clock>>

Valid == leaseOwner # None /\ leaseExp > clock
Step(f, s) == [f EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1, ![(s + 1) % 3] = @ + 1]

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Slots -> 0..Total]
    /\ leaseOwner \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ leaseExp \in 0..MaxT
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT

Init ==
    /\ load = [s \in Slots |-> IF s = 0 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ leaseOwner = None
    /\ leaseExp = 0
    /\ clock = 0

GrantLease(c) ==
    /\ (leaseOwner = None \/ leaseExp <= clock)
    /\ leaseOwner' = c
    /\ leaseExp' = IF clock + 2 <= MaxT THEN clock + 2 ELSE MaxT
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, leaseOwner, leaseExp>>

Advance(s) ==
    /\ Valid
    /\ load[s] > 0
    /\ load' = Step(load, s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExp, clock>>

AdminAdvance(s) ==
    /\ load[s] > 0
    /\ load' = Step(load, s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseExp, clock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : GrantLease(c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Advance(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminAdvance(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conserved == load[0] + load[1] + load[2] = Total
============================================================================

    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl: A car-wash conveyor line arranges a fixed fleet of cars across three cyclic slots, where advancing a car from a slot moves it to the next slot in the cycle. Advancing a car normally requires a valid lease on the conveyor drive: the lease is granted to a single controller at a time, may only be taken when no lease is held or the current one has expired against a shared clock, and carries an expiry deadline. As the clock ticks forward, an outstanding lease lapses. A controller holding a valid, unexpired lease may advance any occupied slot by one position. Separately, a privileged administrator can force an advance directly, without holding any lease, to keep the line moving during maintenance. Because every advance, whether leased or admin-forced, simply moves one car from a slot to the next cyclic slot and never adds or removes a car, the total number of cars on the line is invariant. The full action set is: grant a lease, tick the clock, advance a car under a valid lease, and admin-force an advance. SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of cars across the three conveyor slots always equals the fixed fleet size.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m8p3t0 ----------------------------
(* Power-grid load shedder with hierarchical locks. A load must hold the coarse
   lock on a feeder region before it may allocate any fine feeder slot in that
   region. A load can crash silently, which releases its region and feeder
   locks together. The invariant is hierarchical coherence: any allocated
   feeder is owned by the load that also holds its region, so a feeder is never
   allocated by a load lacking the region, preventing double allocation. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Loads, None
Regions == 1..1
Feeders == 1..2
RegionOf(f) == 1

VARIABLES regionLock, feederOwner, crashed, served

vars == <<regionLock, feederOwner, crashed, served>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ regionLock \in [Regions -> Loads \cup {None}]
    /\ feederOwner \in [Feeders -> Loads \cup {None}]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Loads
    /\ served \in 0..6

Init ==
    /\ regionLock = [r \in Regions |-> None]
    /\ feederOwner = [f \in Feeders |-> None]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ served = 0

AcquireRegion(ld, r) ==
    /\ ld \notin crashed
    /\ regionLock[r] = None
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![r] = ld]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feederOwner, crashed, served>>

AllocateFeeder(ld, f) ==
    /\ ld \notin crashed
    /\ regionLock[RegionOf(f)] = ld
    /\ feederOwner[f] = None
    /\ feederOwner' = [feederOwner EXCEPT ![f] = ld]
    /\ served' = (served + 1) % 7
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, crashed>>

ReleaseFeeder(ld, f) ==
    /\ feederOwner[f] = ld
    /\ feederOwner' = [feederOwner EXCEPT ![f] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, crashed, served>>

ReleaseRegion(ld, r) ==
    /\ regionLock[r] = ld
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ feederOwner' = [f \in Feeders |-> IF feederOwner[f] = ld /\ RegionOf(f) = r
                                          THEN None ELSE feederOwner[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, served>>

Crash(ld) ==
    /\ ld \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {ld}
    /\ regionLock' = [r \in Regions |-> IF regionLock[r] = ld THEN None ELSE regionLock[r]]
    /\ feederOwner' = [f \in Feeders |-> IF feederOwner[f] = ld THEN None ELSE feederOwner[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED served

Recover(ld) ==
    /\ ld \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {ld}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, feederOwner, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E ld \in Loads, r \in Regions : AcquireRegion(ld, r)
    \/ \E ld \in Loads, f \in Feeders : AllocateFeeder(ld, f)
    \/ \E ld \in Loads, f \in Feeders : ReleaseFeeder(ld, f)
    \/ \E ld \in Loads, r \in Regions : ReleaseRegion(ld, r)
    \/ \E ld \in Loads : Crash(ld)
    \/ \E ld \in Loads : Recover(ld)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Hierarchical ==
    \A f \in Feeders : feederOwner[f] # None => regionLock[RegionOf(f)] = feederOwner[f]
============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Loads = {L1, L2}
    None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Hierarchical
nl: A power-grid load shedder allocates feeder slots using hierarchical locks. Feeders are grouped into a region, and there is a coarse lock on the region plus a fine lock on each individual feeder. Before a load may allocate a feeder slot, it must first hold the coarse lock on that feeder's region; only then may it take the feeder, and only if the feeder is currently unallocated. A load can crash silently at any time, and a crash releases every lock it was holding, both its region lock and any feeder slots, together. A load may also voluntarily release a feeder, or release a region, and releasing a region also drops any feeders that load held within it. A crashed load can later recover. Because a feeder is only ever allocated by the load that currently holds its region, and locks are always released consistently, no feeder ends up owned by a load that does not hold its region, which is what prevents two loads from both grabbing feeders in a contested region. The full action set is: acquire a region lock, allocate a feeder, release a feeder, release a region, crash a load, and recover a load. SAFETY PROPERTY: any allocated feeder is owned by the same load that holds the lock on that feeder's region.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m4p5t3 ----------------------------
(* Container-ship crane yard sealing containers. Seal jobs are buffered in a
   bounded work queue with backpressure. A worker claims the head job into an
   active slot, then performs the irreversible seal, appending the container to
   a seal log only if it is not already sealed. The worker may be slow: it can
   hold a claimed job and later abort it. Each container is sealed at most once,
   so the seal log has no duplicates. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Containers == 1..2
Cap == 3
None == 0

VARIABLES queue, active, sealed, processed

vars == <<queue, active, sealed, processed>>

Logged(c) == \E i \in DOMAIN sealed : sealed[i] = c

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Containers)
    /\ active \in {None} \cup Containers
    /\ sealed \in Seq(Containers)
    /\ processed \in 0..6

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ active = None
    /\ sealed = << >>
    /\ processed = 0

Enqueue(c) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, sealed, processed>>

Claim ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ active = None
    /\ active' = Head(queue)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, processed>>

Seal ==
    /\ active # None
    /\ ~Logged(active)
    /\ sealed' = Append(sealed, active)
    /\ active' = None
    /\ processed' = (processed + 1) % 7
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Abort ==
    /\ active # None
    /\ active' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, sealed, processed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Containers : Enqueue(c)
    \/ Claim
    \/ Seal
    \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOnce == \A i, j \in DOMAIN sealed : (i # j) => (sealed[i] # sealed[j])
============================================================================

NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl: A container-ship crane yard seals containers as they leave the yard. Seal jobs are buffered in a bounded work queue that applies backpressure, refusing new jobs once it is full. A single worker processes jobs in two steps: it first claims the head job into an active slot, and then performs the physical seal. Sealing is irreversible: when the worker seals its active container, that container is appended to a permanent seal log, but only if the container is not already present in the log. The worker can be slow rather than failed: after claiming a job it may hold it for a while and ultimately abort it without sealing, returning to an idle state. Because a container is appended to the seal log only when it is not already logged, no container is ever sealed twice. The full action set is: enqueue a seal job, claim the head job, seal the active container, and abort the active job. SAFETY PROPERTY: no container appears in the seal log more than once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m7p5t3 ----------------------------
(* Interbank settlement finalizing payments through a compare-and-swap status
   register. Finalizing a payment is irreversible: a CAS flips the register
   from pending to committed and bumps that payment's finalize count. Because
   the CAS only fires while the register still reads pending, a payment can be
   finalized at most once even though slow duplicate finalize attempts keep
   arriving. A batch reset recycles the registers. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Payments == 1..2
MaxT == 2

VARIABLES reg, fcount, clock, attempts

vars == <<reg, fcount, clock, attempts>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Payments -> {"pending", "committed"}]
    /\ fcount \in [Payments -> 0..2]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT
    /\ attempts \in 0..6

Init ==
    /\ reg = [p \in Payments |-> "pending"]
    /\ fcount = [p \in Payments |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ attempts = 0

Commit(p) ==
    /\ reg[p] = "pending"
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![p] = "committed"]
    /\ fcount' = [fcount EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, attempts>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, fcount, attempts>>

LateAttempt(p) ==
    /\ reg[p] = "committed"
    /\ attempts' = (attempts + 1) % 7
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, fcount, clock>>

Reset ==
    /\ \A p \in Payments : reg[p] = "committed"
    /\ reg' = [p \in Payments |-> "pending"]
    /\ fcount' = [p \in Payments |-> 0]

   stalled vote, but still only through the same snapshot-guarded write. The

    /\ phase = "idle"

    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ phase' = "idle"

    /\ phase' = "idle"

    /\ phase' = "idle"

(* Smart-home door-lock network sharing a fixed set of physical bolts across two
   door slots and a spare pool. A controller optimistically stages a bolt move
   from one slot to another against a snapshot of the config version, and
   applies it only if the version is unchanged; otherwise it rolls back. A
   controller can crash silently, discarding its staged move. Bolts only move
   between slots, so their total is conserved. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, None
Slots == 1..3
Total == 2
Mod == 3

VARIABLES charge, version, pend, snap, crashed

vars == <<charge, version, pend, snap, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ charge \in [Slots -> 0..Total]
    /\ version \in 0..Mod-1
    /\ pend \in [Controllers -> {None} \cup (Slots \X Slots)]
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> 0..Mod-1]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Controllers

Init ==
    /\ charge = [s \in Slots |-> IF s = 3 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ pend = [c \in Controllers |-> None]
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

Stage(ct, f, t) ==
    /\ ct \notin crashed
    /\ pend[ct] = None
    /\ f # t
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![ct] = <<f, t>>]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![ct] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, version, crashed>>

Apply(ct) ==
    /\ ct \notin crashed
    /\ pend[ct] # None
    /\ snap[ct] = version
    /\ charge[pend[ct][1]] > 0
    /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![pend[ct][1]] = @ - 1, ![pend[ct][2]] = @ + 1]
    /\ version' = (version + 1) % Mod
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![ct] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, crashed>>

Rollback(ct) ==
    /\ pend[ct] # None
    /\ snap[ct] # version
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![ct] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, version, snap, crashed>>

Crash(ct) ==
    /\ ct \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {ct}
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![ct] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, version, snap>>

Recover(ct) ==
    /\ ct \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {ct}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, version, pend, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers, f \in Slots, t \in Slots : Stage(ct, f, t)
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers : Apply(ct)
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers : Rollback(ct)
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers : Crash(ct)
    \/ \E ct \in Controllers : Recover(ct)

   reconfiguration bumps the epoch, and slow signallers must refresh their token
   before they can grant again. Late duplicate grant attempts on an already
   entered block are refused. Each block is entered at most once. *)

    /\ sigEpoch = [s \in Signallers |-> 0]
    /\ attempts = 0

    /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % Mod

    /\ entered[b] = 0

    /\ attempts' = (attempts + 1) % 7

(* Smart-home door-lock config log, serialized by a token ring, with a runtime-
   adjustable capacity ceiling. Only the token holder may append the next
   config revision, and only when its snapshot of the high-water mark still
   matches and the mark is below the current capacity. Capacity can be expanded
   or shrunk at runtime (never below the current mark). Appended revision ids
   stay gapless, so no update is lost. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

Nodes == 1..2
MaxCap == 3
RingNext(n) == (n % 2) + 1

VARIABLES high, applied, snap, holder, cap

vars == <<high, applied, snap, holder, cap>>

    /\ high \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ applied \in SUBSET (1..MaxCap)
    /\ snap \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ holder \in Nodes
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ high = 0
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ snap = 0
    /\ holder = 1
    /\ cap = MaxCap

Snapshot(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ snap' = high
    /\ UNCHANGED <<high, applied, holder, cap>>

Append(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ snap = high
    /\ high < cap
    /\ high' = high + 1
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {high + 1}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, holder, cap>>

PassToken(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ holder' = RingNext(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<high, applied, snap, cap>>

Expand ==
    /\ cap < MaxCap
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<high, applied, snap, holder>>

Shrink ==
    /\ cap > high
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<high, applied, snap, holder>>

Compact ==
    /\ high = cap
    /\ high > 0
    /\ high' = 0
    /\ applied' = {}
    /\ snap' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Snapshot(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Append(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)

    \/ Shrink

    /\ regGen = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ pGen = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

    /\ reg[r] = Free
    /\ pGen[i] = gen
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ regGen' = [regGen EXCEPT ![r] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, pGen>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ reg[r] # Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regGen, gen, pGen>>

Bump ==
    /\ gen' = (gen + 1) % Mod
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, regGen, pGen>>

Sync(i) ==

    /\ pGen' = [pGen EXCEPT ![i] = gen]

    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Release(r)
    \/ Bump
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Sync(i)

nl: A hospital operating-room scheduler runs as two scheduler instances that share a single pool of rooms. Rooms are claimed through a compare-and-swap owner register, and each room additionally carries a generation stamp recording the configuration generation under which it was claimed. Each instance tracks its own known generation. An instance may claim a free room only while its known generation matches the current configuration generation, and the claim stamps the room with that generation. The configuration generation can be bumped at any time, which leaves instances stale until they sync. When a stale instance syncs to the current generation, it drops every room it holds that was stamped under an older generation, since those claims belong to a superseded configuration. Rooms can also be released back to the pool. Because a claim is always stamped with the claiming instance's generation, and syncing purges an instance's older-generation claims, every claimed room's stamp equals its owner's current known generation, so no room is left claimed by a stale instance. The full action set is: claim a room by compare-and-swap, release a room, bump the generation, and sync a stale instance. SAFETY PROPERTY: every claimed room's generation stamp equals the current known generation of the instance that owns it.

(* Container-ship crane yard: cranes contend for one berth using hierarchical
   locks. A crane must hold the coarse yard lock and then the fine berth lock
   before entering the berth's critical section, and it cannot release the yard
   lock while still holding the berth. Cranes may be slow between steps. Because
   a crane in the berth holds both locks and the berth lock has one holder, at
   most one crane occupies the berth. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, None
MaxT == 2

VARIABLES yardLock, berthLock, inCS, clock

vars == <<yardLock, berthLock, inCS, clock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ yardLock \in Cranes \cup {None}
    /\ berthLock \in Cranes \cup {None}
    /\ inCS \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT

Init ==
    /\ yardLock = None
    /\ berthLock = None
    /\ inCS = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ clock = 0

AcquireYard(c) ==
    /\ yardLock = None
    /\ yardLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berthLock, inCS, clock>>

AcquireBerth(c) ==
    /\ yardLock = c
    /\ berthLock = None
    /\ berthLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardLock, inCS, clock>>

Enter(c) ==
    /\ yardLock = c
    /\ berthLock = c
    /\ ~inCS[c]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardLock, berthLock, clock>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ inCS[c]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardLock, berthLock, clock>>

ReleaseBerth(c) ==
    /\ berthLock = c
    /\ ~inCS[c]
    /\ berthLock' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardLock, inCS, clock>>

ReleaseYard(c) ==
    /\ yardLock = c
    /\ berthLock # c
    /\ yardLock' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berthLock, inCS, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardLock, berthLock, inCS>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : AcquireYard(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : AcquireBerth(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Enter(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Exit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : ReleaseBerth(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : ReleaseYard(c)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutexCoherent ==
    \A c \in Cranes : inCS[c] => (berthLock = c /\ yardLock = c)

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {k1, k2}
    None = NONE
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutexCoherent
nl: A container-ship crane yard grants exclusive access to a single berth using hierarchical locks. There is a coarse lock on the whole yard and a fine lock on the berth. Before a crane may enter the berth's critical section, it must first take the coarse yard lock and then the fine berth lock; only a crane holding both may enter. A crane cannot release the yard lock while it still holds the berth lock, so the locks are unwound in the reverse order they were taken, and a crane must leave the critical section before releasing the berth. Cranes can be slow, taking varying amounts of time between acquiring locks, entering, and releasing, but they never fail. Because a crane occupies the berth only while it holds both the yard lock and the berth lock, and the berth lock can be held by only one crane at a time, no two cranes ever occupy the berth simultaneously. The full action set is: acquire the yard lock, acquire the berth lock, enter the berth, exit the berth, release the berth lock, release the yard lock, and tick the clock. SAFETY PROPERTY: any crane occupying the berth holds both the yard lock and the berth lock, so at most one crane is in the berth.
